findings.issue: BB re-raise text states 'Our blind and our raise are already in, so the price for one more bet is good' as a plain fact. On route (a), an open and a 3-bet before BB acts, BB has not raised and owes two bets. The closing 'same advice applies when an open and a re-raise come before we act' sentence makes this acceptable under A-8 and §5 rule 5 (main route first). But this sentence is the least hedged of the six re-raise texts, because the 'Usually' in the sentence before it does not carry over.
findings.evidence: §5 route table, BB re-raise (a): 'Cold: an open and a 3-bet.' The UTG–SB texts open with 'Our open has been re-raised' or 'Usually we raised', so the premise is clearly the main route. The BB text follows a 'Usually' sentence with an unqualified 'Our blind and our raise are already in'.
findings.fix: Optional wording tweak at sign-off, e.g. 'When we raised, our blind and our raise are already in, so the price for one more bet is good...'.

findings.issue: CO re-raise folds A9o, A8o and A7o but continues KTo (C*/F) and QJo (C*/F). BTN re-raise continues A9o–A6o. TASK-9.1's locked review test forces the A9o fold (CALL_THEN_FOLD expects Fold). A-4 then forces A8o and A7o, so QTo and JTo were the only sensible remaining cuts. Given that constraint the grid is the best coherent choice and A-4-clean. The CO/BTN gap is also defensible: a 3-bet against a button steal usually comes from a blind with a wide range, and BTN has position on every route. A user may still find 'king-ten continues but ace-nine folds' odd at sign-off.
findings.evidence: chart-print.txt CO re-raise row 9 col A = F, row T col K = C*/F. BTN re-raise row 9 col A = C. tests/table/review.acceptance.test.ts:83-90.
findings.fix: No change required. Optionally the orchestrator mentions the TASK-9.1 constraint when showing CO re-raise at sign-off (SPEC-10) so the user knows it is forced.

findings.issue: Spec §10 mutation probe 1 (set UTG re-raise ATo, KJo, A9s, KTs, QTs to F) does not fail SPEC-02 on this chart. ATo and KJo are already folds (F*/C), so the probe only removes 12 combos (188 → 176, still ≥ 170). This is a stale probe in the spec, not a weak test: removing 20 combos (KTs, QTs, K9s, T9s, JTs → 168) fails with 'expected 168 to be greater than or equal to 170'.
findings.evidence: Mutation run in a scratch copy: probe as written passed SPEC-02. The adjusted probe failed SPEC-02. Adding ATo and KJo as C (212/212) failed the upper bound.
findings.fix: None in code. The judge should use a probe that drops at least 19 continued UTG combos, e.g. KTs, QTs, K9s, T9s, JTs → F.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Q-1 holds in every opener re-raise spot, each a subset of its open set with only premium raises: UTG 188/212 (0.887), HJ 218/254 (0.858), CO 298/358 (0.832), BTN 454/538 (0.844), SB 358/406 (0.882). BB re-raise is unchanged and keeps 100% of U, inside blind-defence. The dropped hands are the dominated offsuit ones: UTG ATo/KJo; HJ KJo/QJo/A9o; CO A9o–A7o/QTo/JTo (forced by TASK-9.1); BTN A4o–A2o/K8o/Q9o/J9o/T9o; SB A7o–A5o/K9o. BB blind-defence has no A-4 inversions and stays in band (46.3%, raise 5.7%). I spot-checked all 26 texts and the chart-level text against the grids and the §5 routes, more than 8 in detail. Re-raise texts (A-8), HJ/CO/BTN raise route (b), the HJ raise-and-calls 'close the action unless a player who limped after us is still to act' wording with the six named aces, SB blind-defence route (b) and the BB blind-defence prices (3.5:1, 3:1) are accurate. chart:print output is identical to doit/TASK-7.19/chart-print.txt and matches the §5 format (no trailing spaces). On the old chart all five six-max acceptance tests fail. Of 15 chart mutants and 7 formatter mutants, all but the stale spec probe 1 and an A-2-permitted BB re-raise widening were killed. Against both main and the base, six-max-chart.test.ts differs only in the D-3 band line plus its comment. No src/advice logic, engine, bots, ui or e2e changes.
